subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Roman Concrete: The 2,000-Year Mystery
description: A quick, practical guide to Roman Concrete: The 2,000-Year Mystery.

hook.text: The Pantheon's dome has stood for 1,900 years. Modern concrete cracks after 50.

buildup.text: Romans mixed volcanic ash, lime, and seawater. They called the result opus caementicium.

discovery.text: Seawater triggers crystal growth inside the concrete. The material actually gets stronger over time.

twist.text: When Rome fell, the recipe was lost for over a thousand years. Medieval builders couldn't replicate it.

climax.text: In 2023, MIT found that hot-mixed lime creates self-healing cracks. The ancient secret, finally decoded.

quiz.question: What makes Roman concrete stronger over time?
options: Iron reinforcement bars hidden inside the structure
Seawater triggers crystal growth that strengthens the mix
A coating of wax that protects it from weathering
